# Python Programming Guide

This document explains core concepts of the Python programming language.

## Overview (section 1)

Python is a high-level, interpreted language known for readable syntax and a vast standard library. It supports multiple paradigms including procedural, object-oriented, and functional programming.

```python
// Example related to overview (section 1)
```

## Variables and Types (section 1)

Python uses dynamic typing. Common built-in types include int, float, str, bool, list, tuple, dict, and set. Variables are assigned with = and do not require explicit type declarations.

```python
// Example related to variables and types (section 1)
```

## Control Flow (section 1)

Use if/elif/else for branching, for and while for loops, and break, continue, and pass for loop control. Indentation defines blocks instead of braces.

```python
// Example related to control flow (section 1)
```

## Functions (section 1)

Define functions with def name(args):. Functions are first-class objects. Default arguments, *args, **kwargs, and lambda expressions provide flexible APIs.

```python
// Example related to functions (section 1)
```

## Classes (section 1)

Classes are defined with class Name:. __init__ initializes instances. Inheritance uses parentheses: class Child(Parent). Properties and dunder methods customize behavior.

```python
// Example related to classes (section 1)
```

## Modules and Packages (section 1)

Import modules with import or from module import name. Packages are directories containing __init__.py. Virtual environments isolate dependencies with venv or tools like poetry and pip.

```python
// Example related to modules and packages (section 1)
```

## Error Handling (section 1)

try/except/else/finally catches exceptions. raise creates exceptions. Custom exceptions subclass Exception. Context managers use with for resource cleanup.

```python
// Example related to error handling (section 1)
```

## Comprehensions (section 1)

List, dict, and set comprehensions offer concise collection construction. Generator expressions yield values lazily and pair well with iteration.

```python
// Example related to comprehensions (section 1)
```

## Async (section 1)

async def defines coroutines. await suspends until a result is ready. asyncio runs concurrent I/O-bound workloads on a single thread event loop.

```python
// Example related to async (section 1)
```

## Testing (section 1)

unittest and pytest are common test frameworks. Fixtures, parametrization, and mocking support reliable test suites. doctest embeds tests in docstrings.

```python
// Example related to testing (section 1)
```

## Packaging (section 1)

pyproject.toml configures modern projects. pip installs packages from PyPI. Type hints improve maintainability and work with mypy and pyright.

```python
// Example related to packaging (section 1)
```
